name: Stride Launcher
description: Auto-updates every launch with no signature enforcement, but all fetches are HTTPS (nuget.org/stride3d.net) — real risk is supply-chain (unsigned NuGet), not on-path MitM. [Opus-verified]
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: The reviewed Stride CLI exposes an explicit `self update` command backed by `dotnet tool update`; its SDK version manager queries the NuGet package store and installs the newest eligible package for a target version line. This snapshot does not establish an every-launch update policy or the end-to-end artifact verification behavior of NuGet/.NET tooling.
limitations: New default-branch snapshot rather than historical release re-verification; package-source endpoint configuration, NuGet/.NET signature enforcement, and launcher startup behavior were not independently audited.

original_evidence.text: | Stride (Launcher self-update) | github.com/stride3d/stride | .NET/Avalonia desktop launcher | Y | Y (`SelfUpdater.SelfUpdate` runs on every launch, before the main window becomes interactive — see `MainViewModel.FetchOnlineData` / docs/launcher/self-update.md) | Y — two paths: (1) normal path replaces launcher exe/`tools/` files in place via NuGet package install, then restarts; (2) "force-reinstall" path downloads an arbitrary `StrideSetup.exe` from a URL embedded in a NuGet package's `Description` field (regex-parsed) and directly `Process.Start()`s it | HTTPS — NuGet feed (default nuget.org unless overridden by `nuget.config`, no override found in launcher runtime code); force-reinstall URL fetched via plain `HttpClient.GetAsync` with no scheme/host enforcement | N — no explicit signature-validation configuration found in NugetStore.cs; relies on NuGet client library defaults, which do not require packages to be signed | **none** in the launcher's own code for either path — no hash/signature check on the downloaded NuGet package contents or on the force-reinstall `StrideSetup.exe` before installing/executing it | n/a — no key referenced anywhere in SelfUpdater.cs | sources/launcher/Stride.Launcher/Services/SelfUpdater.cs:52-63 (`SelfUpdate`); :66-107 (`DownloadAndInstallNewVersion` — `httpClient.GetAsync(strideInstallerUrl)` then `Process.Start(startInfo)`, no verification step); :129-138 (`force-reinstall:\s*(\S+)\s*(\S+)` regex, `installerDownloadUrl = regexMatch.Groups[2].Value`); docs/launcher/self-update.md (documents the same flow, no verification step mentioned) |

fields.label: auto
fields.value: Y (`SelfUpdater.SelfUpdate` runs on every launch, before the main window becomes interactive — see `MainViewModel.FetchOnlineData` / docs/launcher/self-update.md)

fields.label: downloads_and_executes
fields.value: Y — two paths: (1) normal path replaces launcher exe/`tools/` files in place via NuGet package install, then restarts; (2) "force-reinstall" path downloads an arbitrary `StrideSetup.exe` from a URL embedded in a NuGet package's `Description` field (regex-parsed) and directly `Process.Start()`s it

fields.label: transport
fields.value: HTTPS — NuGet feed (default nuget.org unless overridden by `nuget.config`, no override found in launcher runtime code); force-reinstall URL fetched via plain `HttpClient.GetAsync` with no scheme/host enforcement

fields.label: manifest_signed
fields.value: N — no explicit signature-validation configuration found in NugetStore.cs; relies on NuGet client library defaults, which do not require packages to be signed

fields.label: payload_verification
fields.value: **none** in the launcher's own code for either path — no hash/signature check on the downloaded NuGet package contents or on the force-reinstall `StrideSetup.exe` before installing/executing it

fields.label: verifying_key_source
fields.value: n/a — no key referenced anywhere in SelfUpdater.cs
